From the United States Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 race broadcasts in Dolby Atmos format on supported devices. Here are the relevant details.

"Perfectly combining outstanding picture quality and sound to fully capture the thrilling tension of this sport"

Apple and Dolby Laboratories have announced a new partnership that will bring Dolby Atmos technology to Formula 1 live broadcasts on Apple TV, starting with the United States Grand Prix weekend in Austin, Texas on October 23.

Apple stated that Dolby Atmos will work hand in hand with Dolby Vision to "deliver a more immersive viewing experience," making audiences "feel as though they are at the heart of the track, surrounded by the passion, drama and emotion of Formula 1."

Below is the response to this announcement from Oliver Schusser, Apple's Vice President of Music and International Content:

It is worth noting that Apple TV's Formula 1 streaming rights currently cover only the United States market, and no additional monthly fee is required beyond an Apple TV subscription.

Apple previously made the Bahrain Grand Prix available for free streaming in the United States, and has also partnered with Netflix to bring Season 8 of "Formula 1: Drive to Survive" to Apple TV in the United States. Under the same partnership framework, the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix will also be broadcast live on both Apple TV and Netflix in the United States.

Apple secured the U.S. streaming rights to Formula 1 back in 2025, with the five-year deal taking effect from the 2026 season. Apple has also previously expressed its intention to expand its F1 race broadcasting business into more regional markets.

The broader partnership between Apple and Formula 1 also includes "F1: The Movie," which earlier won the Academy Award for Best Sound Effects Editing (Sound) at this year's Oscars, and remains Apple's highest-grossing film to date at the box office.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, and can also be subscribed to through the Apple One bundle. The platform features a wide range of popular series and films, including "Ted Lasso," "Severance," "The Studio," "The Morning Show," "Shrinking," and "Silo."
